rationale: Drytac's current overlaminating films (Weathershield series) offer 5-7 year outdoor durability, while Tedlar delivers 12-20+ years - a 2-3x performance advantage that represents a significant product differentiation opportunity. This role owns portfolio strategy and competitive positioning in a market where Drytac already competes on durability claims. The VP of Product Development would be directly responsible for evaluating next-generation film technologies that could: (1) enable premium product tier expansion with superior warranty offerings, (2) reduce warranty claim exposure from premature failures their current 5-7 year products may experience, (3) capitalize on their recent PRINTING United Pinnacle Award momentum by launching an industry-leading durability product, and (4) differentiate against commodity PVC competitors. Given Drytac's 50-year history and established R&D capabilities (UV stabilizers, anti-graffiti formulations), this role has both the technical sophistication to appreciate PVF chemistry advantages and the strategic mandate to explore materials that could redefine their competitive position in architectural graphics and vehicle wraps where longest lifecycle matters most.

This role bridges technical product capabilities with market demands and customer feedback at Drytac. With active presence at ISA Sign Expo and PRINTING United (demonstrated booth participation in 2024-2025), the Director of Product Management is directly exposed to customer pain points around outdoor durability failures, UV degradation complaints, and graffiti vandalism issues that plague current 5-7 year PVC films. They own go-to-market strategy for existing product lines (Weathershield, Polar Grip Air vehicle wraps, anti-graffiti films) and would personally benefit from a premium overlaminate solution that: (1) commands higher margins in their product mix, (2) reduces customer service escalations related to premature graphic failures, (3) enables positioning against lower-cost commodity competitors, and (4) supports their distributor network with a truly differentiated offering. This role's KPIs likely include revenue per product line, customer satisfaction scores, and competitive win rates - all directly improved by offering Tedlar's superior 12-20+ year performance as either a co-branded solution or white-label integration into their existing Weathershield portfolio.

Drytac operates through an extensive global distributor network serving sign manufacturers, vehicle wrap installers, and architectural graphics producers - the exact channels Tedlar targets. The VP of Sales owns revenue growth targets and competitive differentiation in a commoditizing market where PVC-based films face increasing price pressure. Tedlar represents a powerful sales enablement tool: a premium overlaminate that allows Drytac's sales team to compete on total cost of ownership (fewer replacements over 12-20 years vs. 5-7 year alternatives) rather than just upfront price. This role would care deeply because: (1) premium products drive higher deal values and sales team commissions, (2) Tedlar's extreme durability provides defensible technical superiority against Asian PVC imports, (3) graffiti resistance directly addresses a top pain point in transit, architectural, and outdoor advertising segments where Drytac already sells, and (4) adding a 12-20 year warranty option expands addressable market into ultra-premium architectural and transportation projects currently beyond their Weathershield product capabilities. Given their recent trade show activity and distributor-focused model, this role has immediate channels to monetize a Tedlar partnership.
